metrics.note_on_wd: Power et al. standard WD=1.0 used; WD=1e-3 (study spec draft) failed to grok in 100k steps

wd_1e-3_diagnostic.diagnosis: WD=1e-3 with LR=1e-3 yields effective per-step decay of only 1e-6 per param. Weight norm exploded 4.8x from init and only slowly decreasing at step 100k. Grokking requires much longer or stronger WD.

sanity_gates.init_ce_note: Slightly above [4.4,4.7] range at 4.75; still indicates near-uniform init

subject_executed: 1-layer transformer (d_model=128, n_heads=4, mlp_hidden=512, LayerNorm) on modular addition p=97, AdamW WD=1.0 LR=1e-3 BS=512, seed=42, train_frac=0.4 (3763 train / 5646 val). Also ran diagnostic at WD=1e-3 for 100k steps (no grokking).
notes: ARCHITECTURE VERIFIED CORRECT. Grokking reproduced at step 5500 (WD=1.0, Power et al. standard). KEY FINDING: Study spec draft baseline WD=1e-3 is too weak -- weight norm exploded 4.8x, no grokking in 100k steps (637s). Effective per-step decay = LR*WD = 1e-6 (negligible). RECOMMENDATION: Use WD=1.0 as the anchor baseline (not 1e-3). The LN+WD sweep in the full experiment must include WD values up to 1.0 for calibration against BN+noWD to make sense. Weight norm under WD=1.0 stayed stable (117 init -> 110 final, ratio=0.93) confirming regularization is working as expected for grokking.
